Respondents drawn from a Gaussian copula of the real data

Source: R/copula.R
synthetic_copula.Rd

synthetic_copula() makes synthetic respondents with no language model. It keeps each item's answer distribution and the rank correlations between items, and nothing else. It is a reference generator: A language model that does no better than the copula adds nothing beyond the real data's item distributions and correlations (Lukauskas & Šarkauskaitė, 2026; Kumagae & Kaneko, 2026).

Usage

synthetic_copula(real, n, items = NULL, attempts = 1, seed = 1)

Arguments

real

a data frame of real responses.

n

number of respondents per attempt.

items

optional item table (see behaviour_features()) or a character vector of item columns. NULL uses every numeric column of real.

attempts

number of attempts (independent draws).

seed

random seed.

Value

A list of attempts data frames with n rows and the item columns, ready to be one element of synthetic in authenticity_benchmark() and the other functions.

Details

How it works. Each answer is turned into a normal score at the middle of its category, \(z = \Phi^{-1}((F(x^-) + F(x)) / 2)\), where \(F\) is the item's empirical distribution in real. The correlation matrix of the normal scores (pairwise complete) is made positive definite, new normal vectors are drawn from it, and each value is mapped back to the category whose cumulative share it falls in. The respondents have no missing answers.

Caution. The copula is fitted to real, so it has seen the people it is compared with. It is a strong in-sample reference, not a fair competitor, and it says nothing about a model's value when no real data exist.

References

Lukauskas, M., & Šarkauskaitė, V. (2026). Plausible but not valid: A psychometric audit of LLMs as synthetic survey respondents. arXiv:2608.14606.

Kumagae, Y., & Kaneko, M. (2026). Silicon samples match the answers but not the respondents. arXiv:2610.30900.

See also

authenticity_benchmark() (copula = TRUE)

Examples

h <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ]
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
cop <- synthetic_copula(real, n = 300, items = h, attempts = 2)
# item means of the copula and of the real data
round(rbind(copula = colMeans(cop[[1]][1:5]),
            real = colMeans(real[names(cop[[1]])[1:5]], na.rm = TRUE)), 2)
#>        HSinc1 HSinc2 HSinc3 HSinc4 HSinc5
#> copula   4.53   3.18   3.73   3.48   3.44
#> real     4.49   3.19   3.85   3.60   3.40
